title: How to install Notion desktop app on Mac: step by step, macOS 13 and later
metaTitle: How to Install Notion Desktop App on Mac: Step by Step
description: How to install Notion desktop app on Mac: pick the right build for your chip, open the file, then log in. Needs macOS 13 or later.
targetKeyword: how to install notion desktop app on mac
intro: To install the Notion desktop app on a Mac, go to notion.com/desktop, download the build that matches your chip, and open the file. Then follow the on-screen steps, open Notion from Applications, and log in with your email address.
tldr: Open Apple menu > About This Mac first. A Chip label means Apple silicon. A Processor label means Intel.
Download the matching build from notion.com/desktop. The Universal build covers both chip types.
Open the file, open Notion from Applications, then log in with your email address.
If macOS blocks Notion, click Open Anyway in Privacy & Security within about an hour.
You need macOS 13 or later. Adaptd reports that macOS 12 stops at version 7.38.1.

blocks.text: The desktop app is Notion in its own window. You install it once, log in, and it can live in your Dock. The steps are short. A few details trip people up, especially the chip build and the security prompt. This guide covers both, plus the settings worth changing on day one.
Check your macOS version before you download

Notion's system requirements page sets the minimum for the desktop app at macOS 13 or later. Click the Apple menu, choose About This Mac, and read the version number. If it says 13 or higher, you can install the app without changing anything. If it says lower, update macOS first.

Older Macs need a different plan. Adaptd reports that 7.38.1 is the last Notion desktop version for macOS 12. After that, macOS 12 gets no new features or security fixes. If you cannot move to macOS 13, the Notion web app in your browser is the practical choice.
Choose the right Notion build for your chip

rows: Either, or you are not sure
One file that covers both chip types
blocks.caption: Match the label in About This Mac to the build you download.

blocks.text: Notion's download page lists three builds: Universal, Apple Silicon and Intel x64. The page does not say which one to choose. The chip label answers that question. Apple's support page confirms that Apple silicon Macs show a Chip label and Intel Macs show a Processor label.

Here is a worked example. Say your Mac shows a Chip label in About This Mac. Pick the Apple Silicon build, download it, and open it. If you later see the error 'You can't use this version of the application', you grabbed the wrong file. The fix is covered in the troubleshooting section.
What the installer does and where Notion ends up

Notion's official help says to open the downloaded file and follow the on-screen instructions. That is the whole instruction. Many third-party guides describe dragging Notion into the Applications folder. Notion's own page does not confirm that step, so follow what your installer window asks.

The Applications folder is still the right place for a personal Mac. Notion's deployment guide says the default install location is /Applications, which all users share. A copy in ~/Applications belongs to one user only. Pick the shared folder unless you have a reason not to.
Get past the blocked app warning

Sometimes macOS stops Notion before it opens. Apple's guide for blocked apps sends you to System Settings, under Privacy & Security. Look in the Security section. The Open Anyway button appears there for about an hour after the blocked attempt.

Confirm with your login password. Click Open, then Open Anyway, type your password, and click OK. Notion should open after that. If the button has gone, run the install again so macOS blocks Notion once more, then go back to the settings within the hour.

Skip Terminal fixes you find in blog posts. Some suggest commands that strip the quarantine flag. Those are not from Apple or Notion, and they carry security risk. Open Anyway is the route Apple documents.
What the desktop app adds over the web app

The desktop app runs in a standalone window. That makes it easier to keep Notion beside your other work. Notion's help lists the main differences from the web app. Command Search works outside the app. Notion AI works outside the app. Push notifications arrive for mentions, task assignments and reminders.
The web app has no Command Search. If you want to jump to any page from anywhere on your Mac, the desktop app is where you get that. Command Search also has a shortcut you can change.
Links can still open in the browser. The web app's Settings control whether links open in the desktop app. If a link ignores the desktop app, the troubleshooting section below has the fix.
Set up Command Search and the menu bar icon

Open Settings, then Preferences, to change how Command Search behaves. You can turn it on or off, change its shortcut, and show or hide Notion in the menu bar. Notion's search help does not state a default shortcut. Read the field in your own Preferences window instead of trusting a blog post.

Two more options matter for new tabs. Open Search when creating a new tab sends a fresh tab straight into search. Turn it on if you open tabs mainly to look things up. Leave it off if you usually start new pages from the sidebar.
Notion desktop keyboard shortcuts on Mac

rows: Opens search when the cursor is not inside a block
Opens a search result in a new tab or window
Refreshes Notion and can make a missing update appear
blocks.caption: In-app shortcuts from Notion's search help. Notion writes them as cmd/ctrl, which means ⌘ on a Mac.

blocks.text: Notion's help lists no ⌥, ⌃ or ⇧ shortcuts for the Mac app. Two shortcuts that help with install and launch come from macOS itself. ⌘Space opens Spotlight. ⇧⌘A opens Applications in Finder.
Build one habit first. Press ⌘P instead of clicking through the sidebar when you know the page name. Use ⌘F when the answer sits halfway down a long page.
How to update Notion on Mac
Notion updates automatically, so most people never think about it. To check by hand, click Notion in the menu bar and choose Check for Updates. A normal update needs nothing else from you.
To see when the app last updated, click ? in the left sidebar, then More. Notion's help says ⌘R refreshes the app. If you expect a fix and it has not arrived, press ⌘R and check again.
Admins can turn automatic updates off per user, as Notion's deployment guide explains. Most people on their own Mac should leave them on. A stale app misses the fixes in each release.
Recent Notion desktop releases

Version numbers here come from third-party trackers. Notion's own release index did not show desktop version numbers when this guide was checked. Releasebot lists 7.42.1 and 7.42.3, both dated Nov 4, 2026.

Version 7.42.1 fixed macOS keyboard shortcuts for Command Search and Notion AI. Version 7.42.3 changed how organization settings and creator profile links open, so those links now open in the browser. Trackers can lag, so a newer build may already exist. Check your own version under ? > More.
Desktop beta: opt in for faster tabs
Desktop beta makes tabs faster and lighter, according to Adaptd's report on version 7.39. It is opt-in. Open Settings > Preferences > Desktop beta, or choose Try Desktop Beta in the tab bar.
To leave, click the Beta button in the tab bar. It has a bug icon. Choose Leave beta. Notion restarts each time you join or leave, so save your work first.
Common install mistakes and how to avoid them

The most common mistake is the wrong chip build. The error 'You can't use this version of the application' means the download does not match your processor. Uninstall, check About This Mac, and install the matching build from notion.com/desktop.

The second mistake is waiting too long at the security prompt. Once the blocked attempt happens, go straight to System Settings. Do not wander off to read something else first, because the Open Anyway button only lasts about an hour.
The third mistake is hunting for Command Search in the web app. The web app has no Command Search. Look for that setting in the desktop app's Preferences instead.
Uninstall Notion or reinstall the right build
To remove the app, quit Notion first. Then open Applications, drag Notion to the Trash, and empty the Trash. Notion's troubleshooting says to uninstall first when a build does not match your chip.
Removing the app does not delete your Notion account. You sign in again with your email when you reinstall. Keep the account email handy, because the login screen asks for it.
Is the Mac App Store an option?

Notion's help tells you to download the Mac app from notion.com/desktop. The help never mentions the Mac App Store. This guide did not confirm a store listing, so stick with the official page. A search result that promises a store copy is not proof that one exists.
Who gets the most from the desktop app

The desktop app fits people who keep Notion open all day. Product managers who move between specs, chat and docs get the most from Command Search. Students who take study notes in Notion can use it the same way. See [Notion for product managers on Mac](/for/product-managers/notion) or [Notion for students on Mac](/for/students/notion) for setups aimed at each group.
If you check Notion once a week, the web app is enough. The desktop app earns its place through Command Search, the standalone window and notifications.
Next steps after the install
Open one page you use every day. Press ⌘P, type its name, and press Return. Then check which notifications you get, and turn off the ones you do not want.

Turn on Launch at login only if you want Notion every time you start your Mac. Leave Desktop beta off unless you want to test faster tabs. When you move to a new Mac, come back to these steps and start from the chip check.

faq.question: Does the Notion desktop app for Mac need macOS 13?
faq.answer: Yes. Notion's system requirements page sets the minimum at macOS 13 or later. Adaptd reports that 7.38.1 was the last Notion desktop version for macOS 12, so older systems stop at that build.

faq.question: Should I download the Apple Silicon or the Intel build?
faq.answer: Check About This Mac first. A Chip label means Apple silicon, so download the Apple Silicon build. A Processor label means Intel, so download the Intel x64 build. The Universal build is the fallback if you are unsure.

faq.question: Why does Notion say I can't use this version of the application?
faq.answer: The download does not match your processor. Uninstall Notion, check Apple menu > About This Mac, then install the build from notion.com/desktop that matches the label you see.

faq.question: Do I have to drag Notion into the Applications folder?
faq.answer: Notion's own help only says to open the file and follow the on-screen instructions. Third-party guides describe a drag step. If your installer shows an Applications folder, drag the app there. Notion's deployment guide names /Applications as the default location.

faq.question: Is there a Mac App Store version of Notion?
faq.answer: Notion's help tells you to download the Mac app from notion.com/desktop and never mentions the App Store. This guide did not confirm a store listing. Use the official page to avoid a copy you cannot verify.

faq.question: Do I still need the web app after I install the desktop app?
faq.answer: Many people keep both. The desktop app runs in its own window and adds Command Search, Notion AI outside the app and push notifications. The web app has no Command Search, so the desktop app covers that gap.

faq.question: How do I check that Notion is up to date on my Mac?
faq.answer: Click Notion in the menu bar and choose Check for Updates. Then click ? in the left sidebar and choose More to see when the app last updated. Press ⌘R to refresh if a update seems missing.

task: Install Notion desktop on a Mac
appliesTo: Notion desktop app on Mac, macOS 13 or later, Apple silicon and Intel
requirements: A Mac running macOS 13 or later
Your chip type, Apple silicon or Intel, from About This Mac
A Notion account and the email address you use for it
Your Mac login password, in case macOS asks for it
A stable internet connection for the download

steps.name: Check your chip
steps.text: Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner and choose About This Mac. Read the label beside the chip or processor. Chip means Apple silicon. Processor means Intel.
steps.tip: Write down which label you see. Step 3 depends on it.

steps.name: Open the Notion desktop page
steps.text: Press ⌘L to reach the address bar, then go to notion.com/desktop. Notion's help calls the button Download for macOS. On the page, the link may just say Download.
steps.tip: Type the address yourself. Avoid look-alike sites from search ads.

steps.name: Pick the build that matches your chip
steps.text: Apple silicon Mac: choose the Apple Silicon build. Intel Mac: choose the Intel x64 build. Not sure? Choose the Universal build, which is made for both chip types.

steps.name: Download and open the file
steps.text: Wait for the download to finish. Open the Downloads folder or click the download arrow in Safari's toolbar. Double-click the Notion .dmg file to open it.

steps.name: Follow the on-screen installer
steps.text: Follow the instructions in the installer window. If it shows an Applications folder, drag the Notion icon onto it. Notion's help only says to follow the on-screen instructions, so follow what your window shows.

steps.name: Open Notion from Applications
steps.text: Press ⇧⌘A to open Applications in Finder. Double-click Notion. You can also press ⌘Space, type Notion, and press Return.
steps.tip: Drag the Notion icon to the Dock if you want it one click away.

steps.name: Approve the app if macOS blocks it
steps.text: If macOS stops Notion, go to Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security. Scroll to the Security section, click Open, then click Open Anyway. Enter your login password and click OK.
steps.tip: Open Anyway appears for about an hour after the blocked attempt. Act within that time.

steps.name: Log in with your email
steps.text: Open Notion and log in with the email address on your Notion account. Use the same account you use in the browser, so you see the same pages.

steps.name: Check for updates
steps.text: Notion updates on its own. To check by hand, click Notion in the menu bar, then choose Check for Updates. To see when it last updated, click ? in the left sidebar, then More.
steps.tip: ⌘R refreshes Notion and can make a missing update appear.

steps.name: Turn off launch at login
steps.text: Right-click the Notion icon in the Dock. Choose Options, then clear Open at Login. Notion will stop opening every time you start your Mac.
steps.tip: Skip this step if you like Notion open from the first minute.

steps.name: Set up Command Search
steps.text: Open Settings, then Preferences. Turn on Use Command Search and Show Notion in Menu Bar if you want them. Check the Command Search shortcut in the same window.
steps.tip: Notion's help does not state a default shortcut, so read the field in your own window.

troubleshooting.problem: Error: You can't use this version of the application
troubleshooting.fix: The build does not match your processor. Uninstall Notion, check Apple menu > About This Mac, then install the build that matches the Chip or Processor label.

Go to Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to Security, click Open, then Open Anyway. Enter your login password and click OK. The button lasts about an hour after the blocked attempt.

troubleshooting.problem: Links open in the browser instead of the app
troubleshooting.fix: Click ••• > More > Open in Mac app. To change the default for all links, use the Open links in desktop app setting in the web app's Settings.
Click Notion in the menu bar and choose Check for Updates. Press ⌘R to refresh. Click ? > More in the sidebar to see when the app last updated.

troubleshooting.problem: Command Search does nothing or is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Open Settings > Preferences and check that Use Command Search is on. The web app has no Command Search, so look in the desktop app. Confirm the shortcut in the same window.

troubleshooting.problem: Your Mac runs macOS 12 or older
troubleshooting.fix: Adaptd reports 7.38.1 as the last Notion desktop version for macOS 12. Update macOS to 13 or later to get newer builds.
